statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-62897 (GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6) is an integer overflow in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/434, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none contains the WPF runtime assemblies PresentationFramework.dll, PresentationCore.dll or System.Xaml.dll, or a Windows Desktop runtime pack. What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. None of these packages contains a native Windows PE file. The WPF runtime assemblies that Microsoft lists as affected are built only for Windows and are not in these Linux packages, so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-62897 (GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6) is an integer overflow in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/434, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned the dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and dotnet10-runtime-artifacts packages of the 10.0.8-r0 build for x86_64 and of the 10.0.15-r0 build for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none contains the WPF runtime assemblies PresentationFramework.dll, PresentationCore.dll or System.Xaml.dll, or a Windows Desktop runtime pack. What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. No package of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for either architecture contains a native Windows PE file. The WPF runtime assemblies that Microsoft lists as affected are built only for Windows and are not in these Linux packages, so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-62897 (GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6) is a .NET remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): an integer overflow or wraparound lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime packs for Windows (win-x64, win-x86, win-arm64) as the affected .NET 8 packages, fixed in 8.0.30 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/434, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.30/8.0.30.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder or wpfgfx assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB or smaller) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade that redirects a few types to other .NET libraries and contains no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml, System.Xaml.xml and ReachFramework.xml) in a reference package, which describe the APIs and hold no code; and the WindowsDesktop transport nupkg, which carries only libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs and System.Diagnostics.EventLog) and no WPF code. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file (every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly), and none contains a Windows runtime pack. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.

CVE-2026-62897 (GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6) is a .NET remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): an integer overflow or wraparound lets an unauthorized attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 9 packages, from 9.0.0 through 9.0.18, fixed in 9.0.19 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx4q-gjrx-2jw6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/434, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.19/9.0.19.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB or smaller) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT compiler and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade with no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml and System.Xaml.xml) in the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense reference package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which describe the APIs and hold no code; and the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which carries libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) and no WPF assembly. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.
